summary: This script decrypts a file called secrets_encrypted.md using AES-256 encryption with a hardcoded password, running the decryption tool inside a disposable Docker container to keep the system clean. The decrypted output is written to secrets_decrypted.md in the current directory.

explanations.2: These flags make the script exit immediately if any command fails, prevent using undefined variables, and stop at the first error in a pipeline—basically making the script strict so mistakes don't go unnoticed.
explanations.4: The parentheses create a subshell, which is a separate environment; this keeps any variables or changes isolated so they don't affect the main shell.
explanations.5: The password is stored in a variable so it can be referenced later without typing it out again in the long command.
explanations.6: This runs the openssl encryption tool inside a temporary Alpine Linux container; --rm deletes the container after it finishes, -v mounts your current directory into /data inside the container, -u runs it with your user ID so file permissions stay correct, and the rest tells openssl to decrypt the file using AES-256 with the password.
